english: The Anointed are a cult of psychopaths devoted to Aeron, the God of Body, Strength, Sadism, Lust, Rage, Hate, and especially premeditated Murder. All of its members enjoy violence, and view killing or mutilating the innocent as a most sacred act. Although Aeron is the patron of Berserkers, he prefers the more subtle arts of the most cold hearted assassins. The cult is dominated by small group of powerful warriors called The Occisors. There is not much structure in this religion, although its members are encouraged to attain elite positions in other evil organizations. Aeron is best known as the Lord of Murder. His worshipers are usually terrifyingly powerful warriors, who could easily win most fair fights but pride themselves in never fighting fair. They prefer to strike the killing blows before their targets realize they are enemies. Aeron is also known as Maiden Friend; he has a great weakness for physical beauty, which his worshipers often inherit. They are often unwilling to harm those of great beauty. [PARAGRAPH:2]State religion allows access to:[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_DANAG]Danag the Faithful[\\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_SIR_HALEWYN]Sir Halewyn[\\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_LUIDAG]Luidag the Rag[\\LINK] (world unit)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]Halves the production cost of: [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_HUNTING_LODGE]Hunting Lodges[\\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_GOVERNORS_MANOR]Governor's Manors[\\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_DUNGEON]Dungeons[\\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_PILLAR_OF_CHAINS]The Pillar of Chains[\\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_SCHOOL_OF_SADISM]The School of Sadism[\\LINK] [PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_PALACE_CALABIM]The Calabim Palace[\\LINK][PARAGRAPH:2]Units of this faith are more likely to gain affinity for [LINK=BONUS_MANA_BODY]Body[\\LINK] mana.[PARAGRAPH:3]The Candy Shop[PARAGRAPH:2]Sunlight filtered through the temple's stained-glass windows and cast images of angels and saints on the western wall. Within the temple parishioners shuffled uncomfortably in their pews as the Literal droned on with his sermon. The service was nearly over, and the children were even more restless than the adults. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie sat between her father and her younger brother, Artan. She was nine years old and like most of the children in the temple, was daydreaming about the many treats of the candy shop that sat in the temple's shadow. While others prayed she imagined pine nuts dipped in honey and sugar, gingerbread men and fingers sticky with pecan brittle. [PARAGRAPH]But they would only visit the candy shop if they were good during the service. It was this promise that kept the children quiet and still on Sunday mornings. It was as much a part of the children's religious experience as the Literals welcoming invocation or the brilliant arches of light that crossed the temple's dusty lofts. [PARAGRAPH]Artan swung his feet beneath the pew, risking kicking either the pew in front of him or the bottom of his seat. Amelie squeezed his hand and gave him a threatening look. Around the temple many mothers gave similar looks to their children, and Amelie's was as practiced and effective as any of them. [PARAGRAPH]The sermon closed with a final adulation and the worshipers rose to make their way out of the temple. Amelie grabbed her father's hand and Artan followed quickly behind. Now allowed to talk he was full of questions, most concerning the candy shop. They had been good so yes, they would visit the shop on the way home. And they would be able to pick one, and only one, piece of candy. It was the same as every other week, but Artan and a half-dozen other children still asked their parents if they could go, and still pleaded for more than one piece, though no parent relented. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie remained quiet. She already knew her father's answers and she was trying to pick the candy she wanted from her memory of the candy shops selection. She dreamed of caramelized pears, chewy toffee, or raisins coated with sugar and cinnamon. She carefully imagined each candy as they walked down the hill from the temple to the small shop, and changed her mind at least a dozen times. This was her favorite part of the week. Her father was sober and kind and the three of them were, for a little while, a happy family. [PARAGRAPH]The candy shop was brightly painted with a red roof and white trim over a deep green building. The front door was white, and stood beside a large window which let those on the street glimpse shelves of glass jars filled with brightly wrapped treats. The warm shop was a welcome escape from the chill wind that threatened to bring the winter's first snowfall. [PARAGRAPH]"Remember Artan, don't touch anything. " his father warned, "Pick the piece you want and tell me, so I can ask merchant Hamish to get it for us. "[PARAGRAPH]"Yes papa. " Artan answered. [PARAGRAPH]The shop's front room smelled like gingerbread and vanilla. Other families were already picking out their treats and every child carefully considered their selection, they were stuck between the desire to try a piece of candy and the fear that if they didn't look hard enough they may overlook something new and wonderful. Amelie had a different reason to spend more time picking, she didn't want this brief time in the candy shop to end. [PARAGRAPH]Merchant Hamish wandered over to Amelie as she looked at butterscotch candies in bright wrappers. He was a small man, thin and frenetic, with a weak leg that required him to use a cane. But his boundless energy made up for his clumsy three-legged gait and he made sure everyone in the shop was taken care of. He never forgot an order, and was quick to scoop, cut or measure whatever a customer requested. He wore a red and white apron that matched the color of his shop and had a crazy shock of white hair that would look unusual on anyone else, but somehow fit the shopkeepers wide, smiling face perfectly. [PARAGRAPH]"I have some ginger bread cookies I just took out of the oven. I believe you picked one last week, and nibbled on it like a mouse as you left my shop. " Hamish said. [PARAGRAPH]"I wanted it to last longer. " Amelie explained, "What are the cookies shaped like today?"[PARAGRAPH]"There were some complaints about last week's cookies. Apparently, speaker Ides didn't appreciate having his rotund figure memorialized as a cookie. And I don't know if I can afford to keep making cookies that large. So, I switched to smaller things, like buildings in the city. There are some of the cathedral bell towers, some shaped like the temple belfry, the bridge tower, the lighthouse, and the east gate. And of course. . . " Hamish added after a pause, "maybe a few fat speaker Ides hidden in the back. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie smiled, but before she could reply another family was ready to buy and merchant Hamish was off to help them. [PARAGRAPH]Artan already had his treat, an unnaturally red candied apple. He always picked the largest treat he could find, and today was no different. He sat beside his father on a low bench in front of the window greedily devouring it. Amelie's father gave her a look that meant she had to hurry up. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie finally picked a piece of swirled vanilla and butterscotch. It was so soft she could shape it with her hands and it melted in her mouth. She made tiny bites out of the thumb sized candy as her father paid for it and they left the shop for the short walk home. [PARAGRAPH]Throughout the day Amelie continued to take tiny bites from her candy, and lied to her brother when he asked if there was any left. He finished his apple before they were out of the candy shop. By nighttime Amelie had the last bite saved in the wrapper as a treat for morning and she curled up in her blankets to sleep. [PARAGRAPH]In that grey world between sleep and wakefulness Amelie imagined a bright light in her room. She opened her eyes, but the room was dark. Her tiny bed barely fit in her room, and there was no window. The only light was from her father's room, where a lamp burned. Her door was cracked, and a sliver of pale light bled into her room from the hall. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie closed her eyes and tried to drift back to sleep. When she was again in that strange limbo before sleep the light returned. This time when she opened her eyes, the light remained. [PARAGRAPH]An angel floated above her bed. Tall and beautiful he had skin like honey and light radiated out of him as if the sun set beneath his skin. As wondrous as he appeared his face was lined with concern, and his eyes were unnaturally dark. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie pulled her blankets up above her head and curled beneath them. The angel's light shone through the thin blankets and even completely covered, Amelie could clearly see her trembling hands. But the light was mild compared to the other indications of the angel's presence. A feeling of peace and warmth radiated through the room. And though Amelie had never imagined meeting an angel before, her fear melted away. She lowered the blanket enough to see the angel's face. [PARAGRAPH]"I am truly sorry. " the angel said. His voice conveyed deep compassion and though it wasn't loud it resonated through the small house. "I tried to deliver this message to many people, but they were blind to me. "[PARAGRAPH]"Who are you?" Amelie asked. She wondered if she was dreaming, but it seemed both too real and too unlikely to be a dream. [PARAGRAPH]"I am Verchiel, herald angel of Lugus. I have come to send a message, and a warning. " the angel answered. "Your brother Artan is in great danger. He has left your house and wandered into darkness. He is already beyond my sight, and it may not be possible to save him. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie sat up in her bed. The sudden skip and racing of her heart convinced her that she was not asleep. "Where is he? What kind of danger?" she asked. [PARAGRAPH]"He is within the home of an Anointedor, out of the light and into the province of the god of blood. " Seeing that Amelie was confused Verchiel added, "He is in the home of an evil man. That is all I know. Lugus's influence is waning and I have very little ability to act. You may be able to save your brother, you may not, or you may die in the attempt. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie was already out of bed throwing on her shoes and coat. [PARAGRAPH]"Where is he?" Amelie asked. [PARAGRAPH]"He went to the candy shop. " Verchiel said, and for a second the angel looked afraid. Before Amelie rushed out of her room Verchiel stopped her. "I can give some small help. If you get to the temple and you hold your hand on the altar you will be safe. It is the most I can offer, though it is not much. "[PARAGRAPH]Amelie rushed out of her room and into Artan's. Just as the angel said Artan was gone. His blankets were thrown aside, and his shoes and coat were missing. Amelie went back into the hall where she noticed her room was dark again, the angel was gone. But she didn't stop to consider his disappearance as she ran into her father's room. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie's father snored loudly from his bed. His lamp flickered and cast odd shadows. The room smelled like stale beer and sweat. Amelie shouted at her father, called for him, and shook him. But in his drunken delirium he did nothing but swat her away. Amelie pushed him off the bed. He crashed to the floor in a tangle of blankets, rolled over and continued snoring. Giving up, Amelie left him and headed outside onto a small landing and down the stairs to the street. [PARAGRAPH]It was an early winter night and the season's first light snowfall was settling on the city. Amelie could see her brother's tracks in the snow and she followed them along the street toward the candy shop. [PARAGRAPH]The candy shop was only a few blocks away and it appeared as it did on all their visits. It was tidier than the surrounding buildings, and its red roof and white trim seemed at odds with the fear that clawed at Amelie as she ran. Though the front room of the shop was lost in darkness Amelie imagined that there were still rows of jars full of candy, and for a second she thought herself crazy for having rushed here in a panic. Until she noticed her brother's footprints leading up to the front porch. [PARAGRAPH]She followed them onto the porch with her heart once again racing. The roof kept the porch clear of snow, Artan's footprints ended at the porch stairs. Amelie crossed the porch, and though she had never noticed that the porch creaked in the many times she walked across it, now it seemed to cry out with each step. [PARAGRAPH]Reaching the door, she turned the knob, but it was locked. It seemed secure and untampered with. Unless someone had locked it since Artan went in, Amelie couldn't imagine how he would have gotten through. [PARAGRAPH]Walking down the porch Amelie came to the large front window. Pushing her face against the glass she looked into the room beyond. She could see the vague outlines of the room. The counter where the sales were made, the shelves covered in candy jars. What wasn't lost in darkness seemed normal. [PARAGRAPH]For the first time Amelie shivered in the cold. Though her coat was warm, she had thrown it on over her sleeping gown, which was one of her father's old shirts. It was threadbare before she got it and though it hung just past her knees, it provided little protection against the chill night air. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie walked to the end of the porch looking for anything unusual. At the very end she saw where Artan's footprints began again. He had jumped off the porch and walked around the side of the shop. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie followed the footprints around into the darkness. She had to stop and wait for her eyes to adjust, and build up her courage. There was no one on the street, but as she stood in the shop's shadow Amelie remembered that there was a guard station at the north bridge a few blocks away. If she ran there and if the guards believed her she could be back with help in fifteen, maybe twenty minutes. Deciding Artan may not be able to wait that long, she continued following the footprints around the shop. [PARAGRAPH]The back of the shop was a simple deep green wall with white trim and no doors. There was a small window set too high in the wall for Amelie to see through. But it wasn't the window or the shop that interested her, but what the tracks led to, a simple cellar door in the ground. [PARAGRAPH]The bar that usually blocked the cellar door now lay discarded beside it. Though Artan's footprints clearly led to the cellar door, there was no indication of him walking away. Amelie whispered a prayer to Lugus as she walked to the door, then hoping it was quieter than the squeaky porch, she opened it. [PARAGRAPH]Beneath the door a ladder descended into darkness. Amelie could feel warm, moist air coming out of the cellar and she was happy to see that there was a faint flickering light below. Leaning close to the opening Amelie whispered for Artan, trying to be loud enough so he would hear her, but quiet enough that someone else wouldn't. [PARAGRAPH]After waiting to see if there was any sound or response, Amelie climbed into the hole and down into the cellar. Cellars were unusual in Bourne, as the city sat between two rivers the ground was generally too wet to dig down in. Any sufficiently deep hole turned into a well. But the few she had seen had stairs leading into them, not ladders. And this ladder went down further than Amelie expected. If the candy shop had a basement, Amelie guessed that this cellar would be below it. [PARAGRAPH]The ladder ended at a hallway with a rough stone floor and slick reddish-brown walls. The ladder shaft was so small that an adult would have difficulty squeezing through, but the hallway was much larger. Looking up Amelie could see the night sky, and now that she was on the ground she could see light coming from further down the hallway. After whispering again for Artan and receiving no response she started slowly down the hallway. [PARAGRAPH]A scream echoed through the cellar so pained and shocked that Amelie nearly turned and fled back up the ladder. She couldn't imagine a person could communicate such horror in a yell, and at first thought it wasn't human. But her body went chill as she recognized the voice, it was Artan. [PARAGRAPH]Everything seemed to slow down. The smallest details leapt out at her and even though Amelie ran down the short hallway toward the screams, she felt like she was running in mud. [PARAGRAPH]The hallway continued straight with two open archways on each side. A lit lamp hung on a hook between the archways and provided the only light. Amelie only briefly glimpsed through the first two archways as she rushed by, the left contained large cages, like a kennel. Something moved in the cages, something large and covered in filth. The opposite archway was dominated by a stone table and tools and knives hung from the walls. Both rooms made Amelie more afraid. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie ran into the second room on the right, where Artan's screams were coming from. For a moment she was delighted to see that Artan stood in the middle of the room facing away from her, appearing uninjured. Amelie grabbed him and spun him around, pulling him into a hug. He jumped when she touched him and tried to push away, but as soon as he realized it was her he collapsed against her and burst into heavy, pained sobs. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie didn't have to ask why he was crying. What was hanging on the wall stole any slight relief Amelie may have felt at the recovery of her brother. [PARAGRAPH]Once it had been a man, a massively fat man buried in rolls of flesh. But all the fat had been cut away. His chest lay open, brass eyelets had been sewn into his skin and hooks held open a bloody gaping maw that exposed the bare organs beneath. His organs were tied along his spinal column and his heart still beat from within a thin mesh of netting, his lungs expanded and shrank with each breath and the slick bloody mass of organs dumped down into coiled intestines. His lower jaw and tongue had been removed so his head was a helpless hook on the wall, and his eyes moved and watched the children with an emotion Amelie had never seen before. His arms and legs had been painfully hollowed out, leaving the bone and clinging muscle, but now only air filled the loose skin. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie opened her mouth to scream but no sound came out. [PARAGRAPH]The crack of the cellar door closing shocked Amelie into action. [PARAGRAPH]"Shut up!" she yelled at Artan, "Are you okay?" As she asked, Amelie made sure Artan stayed facing her, so he couldn't see the man hanging on the wall behind him. [PARAGRAPH]Taking deep breaths Artan coughed out his words, "I. . . want. . . to. . . go. "[PARAGRAPH]"We will be okay, calm down. I am going to take you home. " Amelie said. The man hanging on the wall continued to stare at her and Amelie wondered if he had snuck down into the cellar looking for sweets too. [PARAGRAPH]The sound of another door opening and slamming closed shocked them both. It sounded closer than the cellar door. Amelie guessed it was from whatever was straight down the hallway. She could hear someone walking toward them. It was the familiar step, step, click of the candy shop owner's cane. [PARAGRAPH]Holding Artan close Amelie dove beneath the only object in the room besides the hanging man. It was a small end table near the entrance to the room. She could hear the footsteps in the hall. She held Artan's head against her chest and tried to stay quiet. She looked at the hanging man, silently pleading with him to quit staring at where they were hiding. [PARAGRAPH]The lamp light jumped and flickered as someone lifted the lamp off its hook. Then Amelie saw Hamish's wiry legs and cane step in beside the end table. She and Artan held their breath in fear. She briefly considered rushing to Hamish for help. But nothing in the candy shop owner's demeanor seemed surprised by the man hanging on the wall, and that kept Amelie trembling and quiet beneath the end table. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish set the lamp down on top of the end table, and walked across the room to look at the hanging man. With Hamish's back to them Amelie considered running from the room. As Amelie watched, Hamish set his cane down. Then he climbed up onto the hanging man and spun around, sliding his legs down into the partially hollow legs of the hanging man and his arms into the huge bodies hollow arms. Hamish's head came just under the hanging man's upper jaw, so it appeared that Hamish was wearing the hanging man's horrified face as a cruel helmet. The hanging man only offered a muffled cry in protest, but Hamish ignored him. Instead Hamish looked delighted to be settling into the hanging man's body, wearing a living man as a thick fleshy suit. The candy maker's eyes sparkled as he ran a cord through the brass eyelets, sewing himself into the body so that only his head remained exposed. [PARAGRAPH]Too terrified to see what would happen when Hamish finished sewing himself into the body Amelie crawled out from under the end table and pulled Artan behind her. She grabbed the lamp off the end table and ran into the hallway, back toward the shaft up to the cellar door. She pushed Artan in front of her and he climbed up the ladder shaft into the darkness. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie was halfway up the ladder before she heard Hamish thundering down the hallway after them. This time there was no slow click of the cane, only thick pounding footfalls. She looked down at the pudgy flesh of the hanging man's hands and arms as Hamish grabbed the ladder and shook it. But they were almost at the top. [PARAGRAPH]Artan reached the top and tried to swing the cellar door open, but it had been barred from the outside. [PARAGRAPH]"It's locked!" Artan yelled. [PARAGRAPH] The ladder shook again as Hamish was tearing it off the wall. Both the children screamed, hoping someone outside would hear them. [PARAGRAPH]"Hold onto the sides. " Amelie yelled as the ladder threatened to collapse. [PARAGRAPH]"Come down children. " Hamish called, "You will be ripe fruit on Aeron's altar tonight. "[PARAGRAPH]At that the ladder collapsed and Amelie and Artan were left braced in the shaft. Artan slipped on the wet walls. Below them Hamish laughed in delight. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm sorry. " Artan said, and his eyes began to well up with tears. [PARAGRAPH]"Listen to me. " Amelie ordered, "Is there another door?"[PARAGRAPH]"Yes," Artan said, "straight down the hallway there are stairs leading up. But that door is barred too. "[PARAGRAPH]"I don't think so, not anymore. He couldn't have barred this door from the outside if he came down it. He had to have come through the other door. " Amelie said. She could feel herself slipping. Hamish had become quiet, but he still glared up at them with hungry, depraved eyes. [PARAGRAPH]"When I say go," Amelie said, "slide down the shaft as fast as you can and run for that door. Don't stop for anything. Just run and go to the temple, not home. In the temple put your hand on the altar and don't take it off until you are safe, he can't hurt you if you touch the altar. Do you understand?"[PARAGRAPH]Artan nodded. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie took one more look down at Hamish, then she dropped the lamp. [PARAGRAPH]The lamp smashed into the hallway floor and oil splashed out in all directions, burning Hamish and setting the entire base of the shaft on fire. [PARAGRAPH]"Go!" Amelie yelled. [PARAGRAPH]Together they slid down the ladder shaft and Amelie hit the burning cellar floor hard. Artan landed on top of her and she immediately pushed him up onto his feet. The grotesque form of Hamish was slapping at itself trying to put the fire out and though he nearly filled the hallway Artan was quickly up and past him. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie slipped in the burning oil and fell when she tried to run. Her coat caught fire and when she got up again Hamish was on her. Hamish grabbed her sleeve and pulled her against the bare skin of his living suit. Amelie could feel the dank sweat of the hanging man, could smell his rotting flesh and looked up to see two pairs of eyes staring back at her. Hamish's sparkled with dark pleasure, and the hanging man looked equally horrified and helpless. [PARAGRAPH]Artan came running back down the hall. He had one of the knives from the room with the stone table in his hand. Before Hamish turned Artan leapt at him, stabbing clear through the hanging man's back and into Hamish. [PARAGRAPH]The jolt of pain was enough for Amelie to unfasten her coat and slip out of Hamish's grip. She ran by him, grabbing Artan as she went. [PARAGRAPH]They ran past the four archways to where stairs lead up into darkness. Hamish thundered down the hallway behind them and his elongated shadow was reflected on every surface by the fire burning under the ladder shaft. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie could barely make out a closed door at the top of the stairs and she prayed as she charged toward it that it would open. She hit it full speed and it flew open. [PARAGRAPH]Both children popped up into a long kitchen. A pot boiled in a fireplace, ovens were set against one wall and tables were covered with trays and bowls. A tray of freshly baked cookies sat out, half covered in green frosting. The room smelled of gingerbread and vanilla. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie and Artan were stunned by the change in scenery. The room seemed cozy and welcoming, homey in a way their home had never been. But the sound of Hamish on the stairs reminded them they were still in danger. [PARAGRAPH]"Close the door!" Amelie yelled. [PARAGRAPH]Artan swung the door closed while Amelie searched for the bar used to brace it. She found it on the counter nearest the door and raced to slide it through the four iron braces on the back of the door. It had only gone through the first when Hamish hit the door. [PARAGRAPH]For a brief second the door looked like it may hold, but then, in an explosion of splintering wood, the door flew open and Hamish came stumbling up into the kitchen. Once again, the children were off running. Artan threw open the door on the far end of the kitchen, revealing a short hallway that ended at a room the children recognized, the front room of the candy shop. [PARAGRAPH]They ran through the front room, past the shelves of jars and treats they had dreamed about for so long. Artan went to the front door, but Amelie ran to the low bench in front of the window. [PARAGRAPH]The door was locked. [PARAGRAPH]"Help me. " Amelie yelled as she lifted one end of the bench. [PARAGRAPH]Artan grabbed the other end and as Hamish entered the front room the children threw the bench through the huge front window. Amelie and Artan leapt through the shattered window behind it. [PARAGRAPH]The children screamed for help as they ran up the hill toward the temple. Hamish continued his pursuit, and though the glass shards cut up the hanging man's feet, he raced after them. If he had looked crazed in the nightmare of the cellar, he looked even more so in the ordinary city night. A man wearing another man's body as a second skin running through the streets of Bourne. [PARAGRAPH]Despite his cut feet Hamish was faster than the children on the straight road. And if anyone heard the calls for help, they weren't responding. [PARAGRAPH]By the time Amelie reached the temple, her terror had been replaced with exhaustion. She could barely breathe, she felt like she was choking, and her heart was racing so fast it made her dizzy. Amelie collapsed against the temple door and turned the handle, for the first time wondering if the temple would even be unlocked. [PARAGRAPH]It was unlocked, but where Amelie expected the warm glow of safety or an army of priests and angels set to protect them, there was only the cold, lifeless interior of the temple. The pews were empty and the stained-glass windows dark. The clear round window that formed the top of the church was the only real source of light. Through it moonlight shone down on the center of the temple, highlighting the altar. [PARAGRAPH]"Put your hand on the altar and don't let go. " Amelie commanded. [PARAGRAPH]Artan looked less convinced, his eyes widened in fear when he realized this door was the only way into, or out of, the temple. They would be trapped here. [PARAGRAPH]There was no time to try to close the door behind them, Hamish was in the doorway right behind them. As the children ran to the center of the small temple Hamish stopped to look around. It seemed that he may also have expected some sort of defense here, though he was obviously pleased to see that the temple was empty. He closed the temple door behind him. [PARAGRAPH]"For a moment I thought you might get away. " Hamish said smiling. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish stretched in the hanging man's skin, the sight was grotesque and unnerving. Bones creaked and popped and the cord binding the chest together pulled taunt against the loose flesh. Above Hamish's head the hanging man's eyes fluttered back and forth in fear as if looking for something in the room. [PARAGRAPH]"You can't hurt us here. " Amelie said, her hand firmly on the Altar's warm mahogany top. [PARAGRAPH]"Are we playing some of game?" Hamish asked, "Is this your base? I'm afraid I may have to break the rules. "[PARAGRAPH]Hamish walked down the center aisle toward them. [PARAGRAPH]"You dropped this. " Hamish said, holding out Amelie's burnt coat. [PARAGRAPH]Amelie didn't move. Artan fidgeted beside her, he still held the knife with one hand and gripped the altar with the other. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm glad you followed your brother. " Hamish said, "You will make a wonderful offering. And I can keep your brother to fatten up. "[PARAGRAPH]At that Hamish charged the altar. Just before Hamish hit them Artan let go of the altar and stepped in front of his sister, swinging wildly with his knife. [PARAGRAPH]"No!" Amelie screamed, grabbing Artan's free hand. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish caught Artan's knife hand in a fist so large it nearly covered up Artan's entire forearm. Hamish pushed down on the back of Artan's hand with his thumb, forcing him to drop the knife, then with a sickening pop Artan's wrist broke. [PARAGRAPH]Artan screamed in pain. And though Amelie pulled, her brother was caught between them. [PARAGRAPH]Hamish towered over the children, Amelie barely came to his waist and as Hamish pulled the screaming Artan away, Amelie's finger slid easily across the smooth altar. She stretched as her fingers came to the edge of the altar. Just as her fingertips were all that was left of her contact with the altar she let go of Artan's hand. [PARAGRAPH]"Shhh. . . " Hamish whispered to the crying boy. Hamish lifted Artan, placing one meaty hand over Artan's mouth. Three sets of eyes looked down at Amelie, but she stood unmoving, hand once again firmly on the altar. Tears silently pouring down her face. [PARAGRAPH:2]Ceridwen first appeared to a suicidal Kylorin, asking him to worship her in exchange for arcane knowledge and the power to resurrect his wife indefinitely so they might restart their marriage untainted by her adultery. He attempted to make her cult into the State Religion of Patria, but only a small group of elites ever accepted her tenets. The most elite of the elites were the Coven of the Black Candle, whom she tasked with blotting out The Sun. This Coven consisted of Kylorin himself, Os-Gabella, Asmoday, Faeryl Viconia, Alexis, Barbatos, and "Wode"-who was actually the God of Shadow masquerading as the mortal master of Shadow magic. Esus transformed his Seven Aspects (the greatest of his True Angels besides Iaegus) into the Masks each Coven member wore, so that no power in creation could detect or control them. The members could never learn each other's identity, as the animus between Asmoday and the Fey would have made their cooperation impossible. [PARAGRAPH:1]A lesser Masked Coven, called "The Between," continues to this day. It is a small religion whose members are mostly sorceresses whose spirits, minds and occasionally bodies explore worlds beyond Erebus. Many are driven mad by the experience. They refer to their goddesses as the Maiden of the Mask. [PARAGRAPH:1]Among the Sheaim there is a cult filled with a missionary zeal to reach all nations and bring their best and brightest back to learn sorcery without the strictures and limitations placed on adepts by mage guilds in all other lands. They promise unfettered access to secret knowledge of all sorts, but tend to steer their students into the darkest of arts. The Emrys have a goal more grand that blotting our the son. They want to bring on Armageddon and end Erebus entirely. [PARAGRAPH:1]Not all of her worshipers are that evil. The Chainbreakers have more noble goals. They believe the goddess is best served by breaking unjust social bonds. They hate any relationship that is not entirely consensual. Some try to destroy marriages and turn children against their parents, but most focus their radical activism on fighting for the abolition of slavery. They can always be counted upon to provide aid and sanctuary to runaway slaves, but prefer to give them arms and help them slay their former masters. [TAB]Junil, the elder of the Gods, had promised to stay apart from the conflict in Creation. While other gods pressed the limits of the Compact or blatantly ignored it, he held to its restrictions and spirit. Even when his church was a mockery of his dominion, he would not respond. It was only when the compact was openly broken, when fallen angels walked in creation that he responded to help the least of men. He asked only one thing in return: unquestioning obedience. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Order was founded during the Age of Magic, not from divine inspiration but from the growing requirements of the Patrian bureaucracy. The codex of Patrian law had become so byzantine and severe that nearly autonomous inquisitors were needed to carry out it requirements. These inquisitors were magically bound to the codex so that they wouldn't become corrupted by their station. They drew upon the name of Junil, God of Law, in taking their oaths and in carrying out their brutal decrees. [PARAGRAPH:1]These inquisitors were feared nearly as much as Kylorin's Archmages and would come to a city to adjudicate major disputes and to see that justice, as defined by the codex of Patria, was followed. [PARAGRAPH:1]At the head of the church was Soqed Hozi. It is said that if she spoke a lie, reality would change to make it into truth. Soqed had a mute twin who was little more than a dim shadow of her powerful sister. The two remained at the Temple of Atonement where they oversaw the church and its inquisitors. [PARAGRAPH:1]The ideology of Junil was secondary to the church's task of maintaining the laws of Patria. Some lesser confessors began to question: "What was the use of following the law if it was corrupt?". The most conflicted of these was Sphener, an inquisitor who killed demons in his service to the church. He had gazed into hell and it was only his strict adherence to his faith that allowed him to survive. Sphener obeyed every edict of the church, but argued that worship of Junil was the greatest mission of the church. [PARAGRAPH:1]The church found out about the whispered concerns of some of its members and launched the Purge of Whispers, and attempt to execute anyone in the church who questioned church doctrine. [PARAGRAPH:1]The purge was horribly effective and killed members of the church, family and friends. It covered many cities over all of Patria and happened in a single night. Sphener was one of the few that escaped the purge and the next day the church held a trial for him in absentia. They convicted him and sentenced him to death upon the wheel. Condemned by his law, his church, and his god, Sphener came to the church on his own and accepted his execution. He was broken as the church elders and the public watched. [PARAGRAPH:1]Over the next decade Sphener's spirit was seen hundreds of times tending to those in need. He tended to those unfairly persecuted by the church and ministered to church members that prayed to Junil for guidance. This became the basis for the new Order church that would be founded in the Age of Rebirth. [TAB]众神之长朱尼尔曾允诺置身于「造物」的纷争之外。当其他神祇一再试探「圣约」的界限、乃至公然无视它时,他始终恪守圣约的约束与精神。即便他的教会已沦为对其威权的嘲弄,他也不曾回应。唯有当圣约被公然打破、堕落天使行走于造物之间时,他才出手,去援助那些最卑微的世人。他只求一样回报:毫无保留的服从。[PARAGRAPH:2]绝对秩序创立于魔法纪元,并非源自神启,而是出于帕特里亚官僚体系日益膨胀的需要。帕特里亚律法的法典已变得繁复晦涩、严酷无比,以至于需要近乎自主行事的审判官去贯彻其条文。这些审判官以魔法束缚于法典之上,以免因其权位而堕落。他们在立誓与执行残酷判决时,均借律法之神朱尼尔之名。[PARAGRAPH:1]这些审判官令人畏惧的程度几乎不亚于凯洛林的大魔法师们,他们会来到城市裁决重大纷争,并确保帕特里亚法典所定义的正义得到遵行。[PARAGRAPH:1]教会之首是索凯德·霍齐。据说她若说出谎言,现实便会随之改变,使谎言成真。索凯德有一位喑哑的孪生姐妹,不过是她这位强大姊妹的一道黯淡影子而已。二人一同留在赎罪圣殿,统辖着教会及其审判官。[PARAGRAPH:1]相较于维护帕特里亚律法这一教会使命,朱尼尔的教义反倒是次要的。一些低阶忏悔祭司开始质疑:「若律法本身已经腐坏,遵行它又有何用?」其中内心最为挣扎的,是斯芬纳——一位在效命教会时诛杀恶魔的审判官。他曾凝视地狱,唯有对信仰的严格恪守才让他得以生还。斯芬纳服从教会的每一道敕令,却主张对朱尼尔的崇拜才是教会最崇高的使命。[PARAGRAPH:1]教会察觉了部分成员私下的疑虑,遂发动「密语清洗」,意图处决教会中一切质疑教义之人。[PARAGRAPH:1]这场清洗惨烈而彻底,杀害了教会成员及其亲友。它席卷帕特里亚各地的众多城市,竟在一夜之间完成。斯芬纳是少数逃过清洗的人之一,次日教会便对他做了缺席审判。他们判他有罪,处以车裂之刑。被自己的律法、自己的教会、自己的神所定罪,斯芬纳竟自行来到教会,坦然领受处决。在教会长老与民众的注视下,他被碾作齑粉。[PARAGRAPH:1]在此后的十年间,斯芬纳的魂灵被目睹了数百次,照拂着需要帮助的人。他救护那些遭教会不公迫害之人,并抚慰那些向朱尼尔祈求指引的教会成员。这便成了将在重生纪元创立的新绝对秩序教会的根基。[PARAGRAPH:3]将其定为国教后可使用:[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_TEMPLE_OF_THE_ORDER]大教堂[\LINK](建筑)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=BUILDING_LORUM_DIABOLI]魔典[\LINK](世界奇观)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_PRIEST_OF_THE_ORDER]忏悔祭司[\LINK](单位)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_HIGH_PRIEST_OF_THE_ORDER]圣堂主教[\LINK](单位)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_Pontiff]大祭司[\LINK]([LINK=CIVILIZATION_BANNOR]班诺尔[\LINK]独有单位)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_CRUSADER]十字军[\LINK](单位)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_VALIN]瓦林·法努埃尔[\LINK](世界单位)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=UNIT_SPHENER]斯芬纳[\LINK](世界单位)[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=CIVIC_SOCIAL_ORDER]社会秩序[\LINK](政策)[PARAGRAPH:2]绝对秩序与混沌之灰烬、暗流二者均有重大冲突。其一可阻止另一者传入某城,或将另一者逐出。


[PARAGRAPH:3][LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]绝对秩序[\LINK]的祭司与天使,其「阿尔达」受[LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]绝对秩序[\LINK]的影响强化最甚,同时也在较小程度上受[LINK=RELIGION_RINGGIVER]授环者[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_UNBLEMISHED]无瑕者[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]天空的教诲[\LINK]以及[LINK=RELIGION_RUNES_OF_KILMORPH]基鲁莫夫之痕[\LINK]的强化。其阿尔达会被[LINK=RELIGION_CHILDREN_OF_THE_ONE]太一之子[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_MATRONAE]众母神[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_SONS_OF_DISCORD]纷争之子[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]混沌之灰烬[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]暗流[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_GREY_COUNCIL]灰色议会[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]夹界[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_EMBER_LEGION]余烬军团[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_ANOINTED]受膏者[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_STEWARDS_OF_INEQUITY]不公之管家[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]雪之手[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]杰斯议会[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]巨龙崇拜[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_FOXMEN]狐人[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_BROTHERHOOD_OF_WARDENS]守望者兄弟会[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_FELLOWSHIP_OF_LEAVES]绿叶之友[\LINK]以及[LINK=RELIGION_HOUSE_OF_PLENTY]丰饶之家[\LINK]削弱。它在善良领地中会得到强化,在邪恶领地中会被削弱。邻近[LINK=BONUS_MANA_LAW]律法能量[\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_TEMPLE_OF_ATONEMENT]赎罪圣殿[\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CITADEL]要塞[\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CASTLE]城堡[\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_FORT]堡垒[\LINK]或[LINK=FEATURE_HALLOWED_GROUND]圣化之地[\LINK]时会得到强化。它会被[LINK=BONUS_MANA_CHAOS]混沌能量[\LINK]与[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CARNIVEANS_CRAG]卡尼维安峭岩[\LINK]削弱。

english: [TAB]Where the Order values law, the Empyrean values wisdom. Adjudication started from the teachings of Lugus and punishment is not based on adherence to a labyrinthine codex of laws, but from direct consultation on the merits of each case. Social equality and impartiality are the model between a government and its citizens as well as between empires. As such the Empyrean gives equal voice to small empires as it does those that dominate Erebus. One may prevent the spread of another into a city, or drive the other out. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Empyrean was the driving force behind the founding of the Overcouncil. No player may adopt the Overcouncil civic until this religion is founded. Its arda will be weakened by [LINK=RELIGION_CHILDREN_OF_THE_ONE]The Children of The One[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_MATRONAE]The Matronae[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]The Council of Esus[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_GREY_COUNCIL]The Grey Council[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]The Between[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]The Ashen Veil[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_ANOINTED]The Anointed[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_SONS_OF_DISCORD]The Sons of Discord[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_STEWARDS_OF_INEQUITY]The Stewards of Inequity[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]The White Hand[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_EMBER_LEGION]The Ember Legion[\\LINK], [LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]The Undertow[\\LINK], and [LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]Cult of the Dragon[\\LINK]. chinese: [TAB]绝对秩序崇尚律法，而天空的教诲崇尚智慧。其裁断源自卢古斯的教诲，惩罚并非依据一部繁复如迷宫的法典，而是就每一桩案件的是非曲直直接商议而定。无论是政府与其公民之间，还是帝国与帝国之间，社会平等与不偏不倚都是其典范。因此，天空的教诲赋予小帝国与那些称霸埃雷布斯的强权同等的话语权。 [PARAGRAPH:2]将其定为国教可获得以下事物：[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]光辉守卫（单位）[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]光辉战车（单位）[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]喻所祭司（单位）[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB]曙光战士卡利德·阿斯特拉肯（世界单位）[PARAGRAPH:1][TAB][LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CITADEL_OF_LIGHT]光之要塞[\\LINK]（改良设施）[PARAGRAPH:2]天空的教诲与混沌之灰烬、杰斯议会均存在重大冲突。一者可阻止另一者传入某城，或将其逐出。 [PARAGRAPH:2]天空的教诲是上位议会得以创立的推动力量。在此宗教创立之前，任何玩家都无法采纳上位议会政策。 [PARAGRAPH:3][LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]天空的教诲[\\LINK]的祭司与天使，其灵力（arda）受[LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]天空的教诲[\\LINK]的影响而最为强化，同时也在较小程度上受[LINK=RELIGION_BROTHERHOOD_OF_WARDENS]守望者兄弟会[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_RINGGIVER]授环者[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_UNBLEMISHED]无瑕者[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_HOUSE_OF_PLENTY]丰饶之家[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]绝对秩序[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_RUNES_OF_KILMORPH]基鲁莫夫之痕[\\LINK]，以及[LINK=RELIGION_LAERAN_CORD]拉伊兰之绳[\\LINK]的强化。其灵力将受[LINK=RELIGION_CHILDREN_OF_THE_ONE]太一之子[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_MATRONAE]众母神[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]杰斯议会[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_GREY_COUNCIL]灰色议会[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]夹界[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]混沌之灰烬[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_ANOINTED]受膏者[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_SONS_OF_DISCORD]纷争之子[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_STEWARDS_OF_INEQUITY]不公之管家[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]雪之手[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_EMBER_LEGION]余烬军团[\\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]深渊霸主[\\LINK]，以及[LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]巨龙崇拜[\\LINK]的削弱。它在善良之地会得到强化，在邪恶之地会被削弱。它会因临近[LINK=BONUS_MANA_SUN]太阳能量[\\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_MIRROR_OF_HEAVEN]天堂之镜[\\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_SPIRE_OF_THE_SUN]太阳尖塔[\\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CITADEL_OF_LIGHT]光之要塞[\\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_TOWER]塔楼[\\LINK]、[LINK=FEATURE_HALLOWED_GROUND]圣化之地[\\LINK]，或[LINK=TERRAIN_DESERT]沙漠[\\LINK]地形而得到强化。它会被[LINK=BONUS_MANA_SHADOW]暗影能量[\\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WHISPERING_WOOD]低语森林[\\LINK]，或[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WODES_OAK]沃德橡树[\\LINK]所削弱。 \r\n\r\n

[TAB]Kilmorph is the goddess of the earth, She Who Dwells Beneath. She formed children out of stone, the Dwarves, and taught them the secrets of metalworking. One of the first religions available to the men of the world, Kilmorph will answer the prayers of honorable men and even send her soldiers to defend their cities. [TAB]A secret council that is so good at spreading lies that it is often unaware of the truth of its own stories. They have "thrones" (secret meeting places) in most major cities and excel at sneaking goods and people into or out of areas. Esus is known as the King of Thieves, Jack Shadow, and Moonsong, though it's popular for religious leaders to take these names for themselves as well. [PARAGRAPH:2]Founding[PARAGRAPH]This is the most common legend spread about the founding of the religion. No one knows if it's actually true. [PARAGRAPH]Unknown to the other gods, Esus slips into creation from time to time. Most commonly as a traveling minstrel (male or female as it suits him), but occasionally as a merchant, beggar, jackal or crow. [PARAGRAPH]On one of these trips he met Oriol Peregrinus, a priest of Kilmorph who had been stealing from his temple for years. The night before he was to go face trial he sat in a bar drinking and whispering prayers to any god that would hear him, as his own certainly wouldn't forgive his crime. [PARAGRAPH]Esus, who was playing at the bar, overheard him and went to comfort the man. The two shared drinks and eventually Oriol shared his story. Esus offered a lie that Oriol could tell to the church, but Oriol was still worried that he wouldn't be believed. At that Esus offered him an opal scarab that would make anyone believe his lies. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol took the scarab and went to his trial before the church elders. To his surprise, they believed his lies without question. Those that accused him were punished and it increased his standing in the church of Kilmorph. [PARAGRAPH]A year later Esus returned and found Oriol at the bar again. This time he was ruined, he barely had the money to pay for his drink and had lost everything in the world that mattered to him. Esus asked what was wrong and he said that no one believed anything he said. He thought the scarab was cursed and threw it away. [PARAGRAPH]Esus explained that he had made the man's lies believable, but at a cost that no one would believe anything Oriol said that was true. If Oriol told his wife he loved her, she wouldn't believe him. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol sobbed into his drink. [PARAGRAPH]"What is your name?" Esus asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Oriol. " Oriol said, still staring into his drink. [PARAGRAPH]"I don't believe you. " Esus said. "I think your name is Mendax Opacous. "[PARAGRAPH]"My name is Mendax?" Oriol asked. [PARAGRAPH]"That sounds better. That is a name people will believe. " Esus said. "And what god do you worship? Surely not Kilmorph, I think you worship Esus, the god of shadows. "[PARAGRAPH]"I worship the god of shadows?" Oriol asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Yes you do. See how easy this is. " Esus said. "And remember that you can tell any woman you love her, and she will believe you. As long as it isn't true. If you actually love her then your words will be sour to her ears, your affections will poison her against you. You can go to a new city, start a new life, raise up a church to Esus, as long as you know that it is all pretend. "[PARAGRAPH]"I have already lost my wife's love to your curse. " Oriol said. "I have lost my standing in the church, you should have me abandon my faith as well? What if I just go to church elders and tell them about what you have done to me?"[PARAGRAPH]"You could try, but who would believe you?" Esus said with a smile. [PARAGRAPH]Oriol, now going by Mendax, did as Esus suggested and founded the first Aphotic Throne in an abandoned Patrian manor (it was easy enough to convince them that he was the real owner). The traditions of that throne were largely made up by him in a tangled weave of whatever inspiration struck him in the moment. It was said that his biggest secret was that he kept a small shrine of Kilmorph until the day he died. [PARAGRAPH:3]Sects[PARAGRAPH]Every Throne could be considered its own sect. There is no common communication, rules or traditions between them. Some are brutal and vengeful, others are lighthearted and free. They tend to be the opposite of the communities they exist in. Sometimes they are the secret power behind the city government, and sometimes they are teenage adventurers pretending at being a secret organization. [PARAGRAPH:3]An oddity among the religions, the Council of Esus has no temples or ordinary disciples. As a secret society, it cannot be [LINK=SPELL_EVANGELIZE]Evangelized[\LINK] openly to either cities or all the units nearby. However, any unit which is a member can pay to establish a local Council presence in any city. Units without another State Religion prerequisite, and with a leader with the right State Religion, can spend gold to purchase an initiation from an Esus [LINK=PROMOTION_EVANGELIZE]Evangelist[\LINK] on the same plot. That theme, paying for miracles, is common in the Council of Esus. [PARAGRAPH]Esus's priests have the abilities of Spies, including the ability to steal plans, destroy city production, and sabotage improvements including even Unique Features. [PARAGRAPH]State Religion allows access to the [LINK=UNIT_SHADOWRIDER]Shadowrider[\LINK], [LINK=UNIT_DISCIPLE_ESUS]Swindler [\LINK], [LINK=UNIT_PRIEST_ESUS]Thief[\LINK], and [LINK=UNIT_HIGH_PRIEST_ESUS]Propogandist[\LINK] units. [PARAGRAPH]The Council of Esus has major conflicts with The Empyrean. One may prevent the spread of another into a city, or drive the other out. [PARAGRAPH]The Council of Esus was the driving force behind the founding of the Undercouncil in opposition to the Overcouncil. No player may adopt the Undercouncil civic until this religion is founded, nor may any player with this state religion join the Overcouncil.

[TAB]一个秘密议会,它散布谎言的本领高超到常常连自己故事的真伪都分辨不清。它在多数大城市都设有“王座”(秘密聚会之所),尤其擅长将货物与人员偷运进出各地。杰斯被称为盗贼之王、暗影杰克与月歌,尽管教内领袖也常喜欢将这些名号据为己有。[PARAGRAPH:2]创立[PARAGRAPH]以下是关于本教创立流传最广的传说,无人知晓它是否属实。[PARAGRAPH]在其他诸神不知情时,杰斯会时不时潜入造化之中。他最常化身为游方的吟游诗人(男女随他心意),偶尔也化作商人、乞丐、豺狼或乌鸦。[PARAGRAPH]在一次这样的游历中,他遇见了奥里奥尔·佩雷格里努斯——一位多年来一直在偷盗自己神庙的基鲁莫夫祭司。就在他即将受审的前一夜,他坐在酒馆里喝闷酒,低声向任何愿意听他祷告的神明祈求,因为他自己所侍奉的神必定不会宽恕他的罪行。[PARAGRAPH]正在酒馆献艺的杰斯听见了他的话,便上前宽慰这人。两人对饮,奥里奥尔终于道出了自己的遭遇。杰斯给了他一个可以向教会讲述的谎言,可奥里奥尔仍担心没人会相信他。于是杰斯递给他一枚蛋白石圣甲虫,说它能让任何人都相信他的谎言。[PARAGRAPH]奥里奥尔带着圣甲虫去教会长老面前受审。令他惊讶的是,他们毫不怀疑地相信了他的谎言。指控他的人反遭惩处,而他在基鲁莫夫教会中的地位也随之提升。[PARAGRAPH]一年后杰斯归来,又在那间酒馆里找到了奥里奥尔。这次他已经潦倒不堪,几乎付不起自己的酒钱,世上一切他所珍视的东西都已失去。杰斯问他出了什么事,他说如今没有人相信他所说的任何话。他以为圣甲虫受了诅咒,便把它扔了。[PARAGRAPH]杰斯解释道,他确实让这人的谎言变得可信,但代价是:此后没有人会相信奥里奥尔说出的任何真话。倘若奥里奥尔对妻子说他爱她,她也不会相信。[PARAGRAPH]奥里奥尔对着酒杯啜泣起来。[PARAGRAPH]“你叫什么名字?”杰斯问。[PARAGRAPH]“奥里奥尔。”奥里奥尔说,目光仍盯着自己的酒。[PARAGRAPH]“我不信。”杰斯说,“我看你的名字该叫门达克斯·奥帕库斯。”[PARAGRAPH]“我的名字叫门达克斯?”奥里奥尔问。[PARAGRAPH]“这听着好多了。这是个人们会相信的名字。”杰斯说,“那你又侍奉哪位神?肯定不是基鲁莫夫,我看你侍奉的是杰斯,暗影之神。”[PARAGRAPH]“我侍奉暗影之神?”奥里奥尔问。[PARAGRAPH]“正是。看,这有多容易。”杰斯说,“还有记住:你可以对任何女人说你爱她,她都会相信你——只要那不是真的。倘若你当真爱她,你的话在她耳中便会发苦,你的深情会化作毒药,令她厌弃你。你可以去一座新城,开始新的生活,为杰斯兴建一座教会——只要你心里明白,这一切全是假戏。”[PARAGRAPH]“你的诅咒已经夺走了我妻子的爱。”奥里奥尔说,“我已失去在教会中的地位,你还要我连信仰也一并抛弃?我若直接去找教会长老,把你对我的所作所为告诉他们又如何?”[PARAGRAPH]“你尽可一试,可谁会信你呢?”杰斯笑着说。[PARAGRAPH]如今改名门达克斯的奥里奥尔,依杰斯所言,在一座废弃的帕特里亚庄园里创立了第一座幽冥王座(要让人相信他才是真正的主人,实在轻而易举)。那座王座的种种传统大多由他一手杜撰,是他一时兴之所至、灵感交织而成的一团乱麻。据说他此生最大的秘密,是他直到死去那天都还私藏着一座小小的基鲁莫夫神龛。[PARAGRAPH:3]教派[PARAGRAPH]每一座王座都可视为自成一派。它们之间没有共通的联络、规则或传统。有的残暴而好复仇,有的则轻松而自在。它们往往与自己所处的社群截然相反。有时它们是城邦政府背后的秘密力量,有时又不过是一群假扮秘密组织的少年冒险者。[PARAGRAPH:3]作为诸教中的一个异数,杰斯议会没有神庙,也没有寻常的信徒。身为一个秘密社团,它无法向城市或周遭所有单位公开地[LINK=SPELL_EVANGELIZE]传道[\LINK]。然而,任何身为成员的单位都可以付出代价,在任意城市中建立起当地的议会据点。没有其他国教前置要求、且领袖持有相应国教的单位,可以花费金钱,向同一格上的杰斯[LINK=PROMOTION_EVANGELIZE]传道者[\LINK]购买一次入会仪式。为奇迹付费——这一主题在杰斯议会中屡见不鲜。[PARAGRAPH]杰斯的祭司拥有间谍的种种能力,包括窃取情报、破坏城市生产,以及破坏包括独特地貌在内的各类设施。[PARAGRAPH]国教开放[LINK=UNIT_SHADOWRIDER]暗影骑手[\LINK]、[LINK=UNIT_DISCIPLE_ESUS]骗徒 [\LINK]、[LINK=UNIT_PRIEST_ESUS]窃贼[\LINK]与[LINK=UNIT_HIGH_PRIEST_ESUS]鼓吹者[\LINK]等单位。[PARAGRAPH]杰斯议会与天空的教诲有重大冲突。二者中的一方可以阻止另一方传入某城,或将另一方逐出。[PARAGRAPH]杰斯议会是与上位议会相抗衡的下位议会得以创立的幕后推手。在本教创立之前,任何玩家都不得采用下位议会政策;而任何以本教为国教的玩家也不得加入上位议会。
		
		
		
[PARAGRAPH:3][LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]杰斯议会[\LINK]的祭司与天使,其阿尔达会因[LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]杰斯议会[\LINK]的影响而得到最大程度的强化,同时也会在较小程度上因[LINK=RELIGION_STEWARDS_OF_INEQUITY]不公之管家[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_ANOINTED]受膏者[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]夹界[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]混沌之灰烬[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_SONS_OF_DISCORD]纷争之子[\LINK]与[LINK=RELIGION_EMBER_LEGION]余烬军团[\LINK]而增强。其阿尔达会因[LINK=RELIGION_CHILDREN_OF_THE_ONE]太一之子[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_MATRONAE]众母神[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]天空的教诲[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_GREY_COUNCIL]灰色议会[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_UNBLEMISHED]无瑕者[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_RINGGIVER]授环者[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]绝对秩序[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_RUNES_OF_KILMORPH]基鲁莫夫之痕[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]巨龙崇拜[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_HOUSE_OF_PLENTY]丰饶之家[\LINK]、[LINK=RELIGION_BROTHERHOOD_OF_WARDENS]守望者兄弟会[\LINK]与[LINK=RELIGION_FELLOWSHIP_OF_LEAVES]绿叶之友[\LINK]而削弱。它在善良阵营的土地上会被削弱,在中立或邪恶阵营的土地上会被强化。靠近[LINK=BONUS_MANA_SHADOW]暗影能量[\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WODES_OAK]沃德橡树[\LINK]与[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_WHISPERING_WOOD]低语森林[\LINK]会使其增强;靠近[LINK=BONUS_MANA_SUN]太阳能量[\LINK]、[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_MIRROR_OF_HEAVEN]天堂之镜[\LINK]与[LINK=IMPROVEMENT_CITADEL_OF_LIGHT]光明堡垒[\LINK]则会削弱它。
